mainTopic: A vessel's airspace in collecting blood and water, blemishes and age during the blood service, and an animal half outside the עזרה
overview: The amud opens with רבי יוחנן's rule that the animal's veins must be over the vessel's airspace when the blood is collected. רבי אסי asks what happens if the bowl's bottom broke, so the blood passed through its airspace but could never rest there. רבי יוחנן answers from a ברייתא about a barrel under a water pipe. The גמרא pushes back, then explains that רבי אסי really asked two questions. It also brings other versions of the exchange from רב כהנא and רבה. Next comes a משנה about water for the פרה אדומה that flows into a barrel over a hand or leaves. From it רבי יוחנן proves that a vessel's airspace counts as the vessel, and he traces the משנה back to רבי צדוק's testimony. Then רבי rules that slitting the bull's ear before קבלה disqualifies it, and רבא brings a ברייתא extending the rule to קדשים קלים. After אביי's challenge, that ברייתא is limited to the age rule, which shows that age in קדשים is counted to the hour. The amud ends with רבי אלעזר's case of an animal inside the עזרה whose legs are outside.

steps.title: Support for bringing the veins into the vessel
steps.stepSummary: The previous ruling ends with the requirement to bring the veins into the vessel. A statement of רבי יוחנן is quoted that supports it: the veins must 'see' the vessel's airspace.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The priest must bring] the veins into the vessel. It was also stated: רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the veins must see the airspace of the vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ruling from just before: the veins of the slaughtered animal must be brought into the vessel. It then brings a statement from רבי יוחנן that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood must go straight from the animal into the כלי for proper קבלה. רבי יוחנן's wording explains what 'into the vessel' means. The veins don't have to touch the vessel, but they must be over its open space, so the blood enters the vessel's airspace right away.

keyTerms.meaning: The neck veins of the animal, from which the blood flows at slaughter
The service vessel used to collect the blood
'It was also stated': another statement that supports the ruling

phrases.english: the veins into the vessel.
It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The veins must see the airspace of the vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends and supports the ruling from the previous section about putting the veins into the vessel.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the veins must be brought into the vessel during קבלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אסי quoting רבי יוחנן: the veins must see the vessel's airspace
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that entering the vessel's airspace counts for collecting blood. That idea sets up the question that comes next.

steps.title: Blood passing through a broken bowl
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי asks: the bowl's bottom broke, and then the blood entered its airspace and fell through. Does the blood count as having rested in the vessel?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי asked רבי יוחנן: If the priest was collecting, and the bottom of the bowl broke before the blood reached its airspace, what is the law? Is airspace where the blood will never come to rest treated as if the blood rested there, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי asks a question. Blood entered the bowl's airspace, but the bowl had no bottom, so the blood fell straight through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the vessel's airspace matters. Here the blood was in that airspace but could never actually rest in the bowl. If the airspace counts as 'inside', the blood was already collected and stays כשר. If it does not count, the blood spilled straight to the floor and is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him; introduces a question put to a teacher
The bowl used to collect and throw the blood
Airspace where the liquid will never come to rest
Is it treated as if it is resting there?

steps.confusionAlert: The bottom broke FIRST. The blood never sat in a whole bowl even for a moment. It only passed through the bowl's space.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:
If he was collecting, and the bottom of the bowl broke

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ דָּם לַאֲוִיר – מַהוּ?
phrases.english: before the blood reached the airspace, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Picture it: the bottom breaks, then the blood enters the bowl's space and falls right out the hole.

phrases.english: Airspace in which it will not end up resting:

phrases.aramaic: כְּמוּנָּח דָּמֵי, אוֹ לָא כְּמוּנָּח דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: is it considered as resting, or is it not considered as resting?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that the vessel's airspace counts, and asks about airspace where the blood can never rest.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does blood that enters a vessel's airspace count as collected, even when it can never come to rest in the vessel?

steps.title: The barrel under the water pipe
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers with a ברייתא. Water falling into a barrel's airspace already counts as being in the barrel, unless the barrel is attached to the pipe.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it. A barrel placed under a pipe: the water inside it and the water outside it are both unfit. If he attached the barrel's mouth to the pipe, the water inside is unfit, but the water outside is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tries to answer the question from a ברייתא about a barrel catching water from a pipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the barrel just sits under the pipe, the water still falling through the barrel's airspace is already treated as being in the barrel. That is why it is unfit along with the water inside. When the barrel is attached to the pipe, the water still in the pipe is not in the barrel's airspace, so it stays fit. The lesson: entering a vessel's airspace counts as being in the vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: You have learned it: the answer is in a known source
A pipe or spout from which water pours

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
A barrel that is placed under the pipe:
the water inside it and the water outside it are unfit.
phrases.notes: 'Outside it' means water still falling through the air above the barrel, not yet inside.

phrases.english: If he joined its mouth to the pipe:
the water inside it is unfit,
and the water outside it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אסי's question by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A vessel's airspace counts as inside the vessel, so blood that entered the bowl's airspace should count as collected.

steps.title: The barrel case does not answer the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In the barrel case the water will end up resting in the barrel. רבי אסי asked about airspace where the blood can never rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? He asked him about airspace where it will never come to rest, and he answers him from airspace where it will come to rest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יוחנן's answer and says the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The barrel has a bottom, so the falling water is about to land and stay there. Treating it as already inside makes sense. The broken bowl has no bottom, so the blood can never stay. The ברייתא doesn't tell us how to treat that kind of airspace. Step 5 answers this objection.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? Introduces a rejection of a comparison
Airspace where the liquid will end up resting

steps.whatToRemember: Two kinds of airspace: one where the liquid will land and stay (the barrel), and one where it will never rest (the broken bowl). The ברייתא only proves the first counts as 'inside'. רבי אסי's question about the second is still open.

phrases.english: What is this?

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ – אֲוִיר שֶׁאֵין סוֹפוֹ לָנוּחַ;
phrases.english: He asks him about airspace in which it will not end up resting,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָא פָשֵׁט לֵיהּ אֲוִיר שֶׁסּוֹפוֹ לָנוּחַ!
phrases.english: and he resolves it for him with airspace in which it will end up resting!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the barrel ברייתא to answer רבי אסי's question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The barrel is airspace where the water will come to rest, but the broken bowl is airspace where the blood never can. The cases are different.

steps.title: רבי אסי actually asked two questions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the rejection: רבי אסי asked two questions, and the second one, about airspace where the liquid will end up resting, is exactly what the barrel ברייתא answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was asking him two things. If you will say that airspace where the liquid will never end up resting does not count as resting, what about airspace where it will end up resting?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves רבי יוחנן's proof. רבי אסי asked a second question that the barrel ברייתא fits perfectly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the barrel case does not match the broken bowl, because in the barrel the water will end up resting. Now the גמרא explains that רבי אסי had a second question about exactly that kind of airspace. So the ברייתא answers the second question, even if the first question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: if you will say / if you decide that... (introduces a follow-up question)
airspace (the empty space inside a vessel)
it will end up resting (inside the vessel)
it is considered as if resting there

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not answer the first question, about the broken bowl. It answers only the second question, where the liquid will end up resting.

phrases.english: He was asking him two things;
if you will say:
airspace where it will not end up resting
is not considered as resting,
phrases.notes: This first part is the broken-bowl case from Step 2, where the blood falls right through.

phrases.english: airspace where it will end up resting, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in Step 4 by changing how we understand רבי אסי's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the question: there were two questions, and the proof answers the second.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אסי asked only about airspace where the blood never rests, so the barrel ברייתא does not fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אסי also asked about airspace where the liquid will rest, and the barrel ברייתא answers that it counts as inside the vessel.

steps.title: רב יוסף's version and רב כהנא's version
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches the exchange as we just learned it. רב כהנא teaches that רבי אסי asked directly about a barrel, and רבי יוחנן answered with the barrel ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף teaches it this way. רב כהנא teaches: he asked him about a barrel, and he answered him with a barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that other אמוראים told this conversation differently. In רב כהנא's version, the question and the answer were both about the barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יוסף's version, the question began with the bowl and needed the 'two questions' explanation. In רב כהנא's version, there is no problem at all: רבי אסי asked about water in a barrel's airspace, and רבי יוחנן quoted the ברייתא that rules on exactly that.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef teaches it this way.
Rav Kahana teaches:
He asked him about a barrel,
and he resolved it for him with a barrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף מַתְנֵי הָכִי. רַב כָּהֲנָא מַתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Labels the version just learned as רב יוסף's and offers another way of telling the exchange.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב כהנא's version, רבי אסי asked about water in a barrel's airspace, and רבי יוחנן answered with the barrel ברייתא.

steps.title: רבה's version: proving it from the bowl
steps.stepSummary: רבה teaches that רבי אסי asked about a barrel, and רבי יוחנן answered from the מזרק: blood always flies through the air into the bowl, so airspace must count as inside the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה teaches: he asked him about a barrel, and he answered him from a bowl. Don't you agree about a bowl, that it is impossible to collect blood in it without a spurt?
steps.whatsHappening: A third version: the question is about the barrel, but the answer comes from simple logic about collecting blood in the מזרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an animal is slaughtered, the blood shoots through the air before it lands in the bowl. If the bowl's airspace did not count as part of the bowl, no blood could ever be properly collected. So airspace must count as inside the vessel, and the same is true for the barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: the bowl used to collect blood in the בית המקדש
a spurt or stream (of blood shooting out)

steps.whyThisMatters: This version shows that the idea that a vessel's airspace counts as the vessel is built into the everyday עבודה in the בית המקדש, not only learned from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabba teaches:
He asked him about a barrel,
and he resolved it for him from a bowl:
Don't you agree regarding a bowl,
that it is impossible for it without a spurt?!
phrases.notes: The blood always shoots through the air first, so the bowl's airspace has to count.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה מַתְנֵי: חָבִית בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ, וּפְשַׁט לֵיהּ מִזְרָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third version of the exchange, with a different source for the answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vessel's airspace counts as the vessel, as we see from the מזרק, which always receives blood through the air.
steps.whatToRemember: In all versions, liquid in a vessel's airspace that will end up resting there counts as already inside the vessel. The versions differ only in what was asked and how it was proven.

steps.title: A משנה: water passing through objects into the barrel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if water for מי חטאת flows into the barrel through something that can become impure, it is disqualified; through something that cannot become impure, it is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: If someone placed his hand, his foot, or vegetable leaves so that water would pass into the barrel, the water is disqualified. Reed leaves or nut leaves: it is fit. This is the rule: something that can become impure disqualifies; something that cannot become impure leaves it fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about water flowing into the barrel. It is setting up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water must go into the barrel directly. A hand or vegetable leaves can become impure (מקבל טומאה), so water passing over them is disqualified. Reed and nut leaves cannot become impure, so they do not ruin the water.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in מסכת פרה, about the water used with the ashes of the פרה אדומה.

phrases.english: If he placed his hand or his foot
or vegetable leaves
so that water would pass into the barrel,
they are disqualified.
Reed leaves and nut leaves: it is fit.
This is the rule:
something that can become impure: disqualified,
something that cannot become impure: fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the barrel ברייתא to a related משנה about how water reaches the barrel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water flowing into the barrel through an object that can become impure is disqualified. Through an object that cannot become impure, it stays fit.

steps.title: Where does this rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the barrel משנה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule it just quoted: why does it matter whether the water flowed through something that can become impure? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 8 says the path the water takes into the barrel decides whether it is fit. That is a surprising rule, so the גמרא wants a פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the barrel משנה quoted in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that the way water is gathered into the vessel must not go through something that can become impure.

steps.title: The source: a gathering of water must come about through purity
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי יוסי בר אבא, learns from a פסוק that the gathering of the water must happen through pure things.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בר אבא: the פסוק says, "Nevertheless a spring or a pit, a gathering of water, shall be pure." This means that the way the water comes into being must be through purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק. The water's gathering, meaning how it got into the vessel, has to happen through things that cannot become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "shall be pure" are read as describing the process of gathering, not only the water itself. So if the water passed through something that can become impure on its way in, the gathering was not done 'through purity,' and the water is disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: their coming into being (how the water got gathered)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan says in the name of Rabbi Yosei bar Abba:
The verse states:
"Nevertheless a spring or a pit,
a gathering of water, shall be pure"
their coming into being must be by way of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'a gathering of water shall be pure' teaches that the water's gathering must take place through things that cannot become impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the path of the water matters at all. That is what makes the next inference about airspace possible.

steps.title: The airspace of a vessel counts as the vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the barrel משנה that the air above a vessel is treated like the vessel itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This teaches that the airspace of a vessel is considered like the vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן draws a conclusion from the barrel משנה: the air above a vessel counts as part of the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water flows off a hand, which can become impure, and then falls through the air into the barrel, yet the משנה still disqualifies it. That only makes sense if the water was already 'in the barrel' the moment it entered the air above it, straight from the hand. Otherwise the last thing it passed through before entering would be plain air, which cannot become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: this teaches (a conclusion drawn from a source)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
That is to say,
phrases.notes: "This" is the barrel משנה from step 8, where the water runs over a hand and into the barrel.

phrases.english: the airspace of a vessel is considered like the vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת, אֲוִיר כְּלִי כִּכְלִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the barrel משנה, whose source was just established.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The airspace of a vessel counts as the vessel itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This matches the barrel ברייתא from step 3: liquid in the airspace that will land in the vessel counts as inside it. This משנה reaches the same rule from a different direction.

steps.title: Maybe the water just trickles straight in
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא suggests the משנה may describe water trickling directly from the hand into the barrel with no air in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי חייא בר אבא: But perhaps the case is where the water trickles?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the proof. Maybe the hand rests right on the rim, so the water trickles straight into the barrel without ever passing through air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there is no gap of air, the water goes directly from the hand into the barrel. Then the משנה teaches nothing about airspace, and רבי יוחנן's conclusion falls away.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
But perhaps it is where the water trickles?
phrases.notes: He means the hand sits on the barrel's edge, so the water slides straight in without falling through any air.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 11 by reinterpreting the case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's inference that airspace counts as the vessel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the water trickles directly from hand to barrel, it never passes through air, so the משנה proves nothing about airspace.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה shows the water passes through the air
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא answers sharply: the משנה says 'so that water will pass to the barrel,' which describes a flowing stream.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Fool! We learned 'so that the water will pass to the barrel'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא rejects רבי זירא's suggestion by pointing to the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'so that water will pass to the barrel' describes water traveling as a stream toward the barrel. That means it crosses through the air before landing. So the trickling reading does not fit the משנה, and the proof about airspace stands.

phrases.english: He said to him: Imbecile!
phrases.notes: Literally "beet." It's a sharp jab, something like calling him a blockhead.

phrases.english: "In order that water will pass to the barrel"
we learned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 12 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The water might trickle straight from the hand into the barrel with no air in between.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה describes water passing as a stream into the barrel, so it crosses the air. Airspace therefore counts as the vessel.
steps.whatToRemember: From the barrel משנה, רבי יוחנן proves that a vessel's airspace counts as the vessel. The משנה's words 'so that water will pass to the barrel' rule out the trickling reading.

steps.title: The barrel משנה comes from רבי צדוק's testimony
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the barrel משנה was taught on the basis of רבי צדוק's testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This משנה was taught from the testimony of רבי צדוק.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds historical background: the barrel משנה is based on an older testimony from רבי צדוק. The גמרא is about to quote that testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is new information about where the משנה's rule originally came from. It is not another challenge. It sets up the quote of רבי צדוק's testimony in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: testimony about an earlier ruling or tradition

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba says that Rabbi Yochanan says:
From the testimony of Rabbi Tzadok
this mishna was taught;

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעֵדוּתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי צָדוֹק נִישְׁנֵית מִשְׁנָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from analyzing the barrel משנה to explaining its historical origin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The barrel משנה is based on רבי צדוק's testimony.

steps.title: רבי צדוק's testimony about water channeled through nut leaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in עדיות: water channeled through nut leaves is fit, and the Sages in לשכת הגזית agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי צדוק testified about streams that someone channeled through nut leaves, that the water is fit. This happened in אוהליא, and the case came before the Sages in לשכת הגזית, and they declared it fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי צדוק's testimony to show where the barrel משנה comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nut leaves cannot become impure. So water channeled through them stays fit, which matches the second half of the barrel משנה: water that flows through something that cannot become impure is fit. The Sages of לשכת הגזית accepted this ruling in an actual case.

keyTerms.meaning: the Chamber of Hewn Stone, where the Sanhedrin sat in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Rabbi Tzadok testified about flowing streams
that one channeled through leaves of nut trees
phrases.notes: Nut leaves can't become impure. That's the 'cannot become impure' half of the barrel משנה.

phrases.english: that they are fit;
this was an incident in Ohalya,
and the incident came before the Sages
in the Chamber of Hewn Stone,
and they deemed it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הֵעִיד רַבִּי צָדוֹק עַל הַזּוֹחֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the testimony that step 14 named as the origin of the barrel משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the barrel משנה is based on רבי צדוק's testimony.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה עדיות: רבי צדוק testified that water channeled through nut leaves is fit, and the Sages in לשכת הגזית agreed.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'fit' half of the barrel משנה goes back to an actual case. Water was channeled through nut leaves, which cannot become impure, and the Sages ruled it fit.

steps.title: Slitting the bull's ear before collecting the blood disqualifies it
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes רבי: if the bull's ear is slit after שחיטה and the blood is collected afterward, the קרבן is פסול, because the פסוק says 'the blood of the bull.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבי: if someone slits the ear of the bull and only afterward collects its blood, the offering is disqualified. The פסוק says 'And he shall take from the blood of the bull,' meaning a bull as it already was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling from רבי. A blemish made after שחיטה but before the blood is collected makes the קרבן פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the animal is slaughtered, you might think a new blemish no longer matters. רבי says it does matter. The פסוק still calls it 'the bull' when the blood is collected, so it must be the same unblemished bull it was before.

keyTerms.meaning: one who slits or cuts (here, the ear), which creates a מום
collected its blood (קבלה), one of the blood services
a bull as it already was, meaning still whole and without a blemish

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows that a blemish after שחיטה still matters, at least until קבלה. The next steps look for the same rule for קדשים קלים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rebbi said:
One who slits the ear of the bull,
phrases.notes: This happens after the שחיטה, and the slit ear counts as a blemish.

phrases.english: and afterward collected its blood: it is disqualified;
as it is said: "And he shall take from the blood of the bull"
a bull that is as it already was.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from רבי יוחנן's discussion of the barrel and the testimony of רבי צדוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A blemish made after שחיטה but before קבלה disqualifies the קרבן, learned from the word 'הפר' in ויקרא 4:5.

steps.title: Where do we learn this for offerings of lesser sanctity?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about the bull deals with קדשי קדשים. The גמרא asks where we learn the same rule for קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for offerings of the most sacred order. From where do we know it for offerings of lesser sanctity?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the proof covers only one kind of קרבן and asks for a source for the other kind. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פר in ויקרא 4 is a קרבן of the most sacred order. A rule learned from it might be limited to that holier level. So the גמרא needs a separate source for קדשים קלים.

keyTerms.meaning: offerings of the most sacred order
from where do we know it?

phrases.english: We have found a source for offerings of the most sacred order;
for offerings of lesser sanctity, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים; קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי's rule reaches, beyond the kind of קרבן his פסוק talks about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a blemish after שחיטה also disqualifies קדשים קלים.

steps.title: The פסח must stay unblemished through every blood service
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא about the קרבן פסח: the word 'יהיה' teaches that the animal must be תמים and in its first year during שחיטה, קבלה, הולכה and זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said that a ברייתא teaches: 'A lamb without blemish, a male of the first year' means it must be unblemished and in its first year at the time of שחיטה. From where do we know this also applies at קבלה, הולכה and זריקה? The פסוק says 'it shall be,' meaning every stage must take place only while it is unblemished and in its first year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question with a ברייתא about the קרבן פסח, which is one of the קדשים קלים. The animal must stay whole through all the blood services.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'שה תמים' by themselves would only require the animal to be whole at שחיטה. The extra word 'יהיה' stretches the requirement to every stage of the service. Since the פסח is from the קדשים קלים, this gives the source the previous step asked for.

keyTerms.meaning: carrying the blood to the מזבח
sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
all its stages (every step of its service)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's ברייתא learns from 'יהיה' that the פסח must be תמים and בן שנה at every blood service. Step 20 narrows this so that only the בן שנה part runs through זריקה.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is taught in a baraita:
"A lamb without blemish, a male of the first year":
phrases.notes: שמות 12:5. This פסוק is about the קרבן פסח, which is from the קדשים קלים.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא תָּמִים וּבֶן שָׁנָה בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה.
phrases.english: meaning it must be unblemished and in its first year at the time of slaughter.
At collection, at carrying, at sprinkling: from where do we know it?
The verse teaches: "It shall be":
phrases.notes: Later in the same פסוק: 'יהיה לכם', it shall be for you.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הֲוָייוֹתָיו לֹא יִהְיוּ אֶלָּא תָּם וּבֶן שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: all its stages must take place only while it is unblemished and in its first year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by bringing a source that deals with a קרבן from the קדשים קלים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא on the קרבן פסח learns from 'יהיה' that the animal must be תמים during קבלה, הולכה and זריקה.

steps.title: אביי objects: only a כזית needs to be left to sprinkle the blood
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רבי יהושע: for any קרבן, if a כזית of meat or fat is left, the blood is sprinkled. This suggests that damage to the animal does not stop the blood service.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised an objection: רבי יהושע says that for all the offerings in the תורה, if an olive's worth of meat or an olive's worth of fat is left, the כהן sprinkles the blood!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the rule that a blemish before the blood service disqualifies the קרבן. He uses a ברייתא in which רבי יהושע allows sprinkling the blood even when most of the animal is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a small blemish like a slit ear disqualifies the קרבן, it is hard to see how the blood could be sprinkled when only a כזית is left. רבי יהושע seems to say the animal does not need to stay whole for זריקה. That seems to contradict רבי and רבא's ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: an olive's worth, a minimum amount
the fats that are burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע doesn't mention a blemish at all. אביי's point is this: if the blood can be sprinkled when almost the whole animal is gone, the animal surely doesn't need to stay תמים until זריקה.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
All the offerings in the Torah
from which an olive's worth of meat is left

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כְּזַיִת חֵלֶב – זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם!
phrases.english: or an olive's worth of fat: he sprinkles the blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule set up in steps 16 and 18 by bringing an opposing ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the animal must stay unblemished until קבלה, הולכה and זריקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע allows זריקה when only a כזית of meat or fat is left. That implies the animal does not need to stay whole until the blood is sprinkled.

steps.title: The verse only teaches the rule of being in its first year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers אביי by saying the derivation from 'יהיה' only requires the animal to be בן שנה through זריקה, not that it stay תמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain the verse as being only about the animal being in its first year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge by narrowing what the ברייתא of רבא actually teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי showed from רבי יהושע that damage to the animal does not stop the blood service, so the animal does not need to stay תמים until זריקה. The גמרא agrees and says the word 'יהיה' only teaches that it must still be בן שנה during all four blood services. So the תמים part is dropped, and only the age rule stays.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain it as / interpret it as

phrases.english: Interpret it as referring to being in its first year.
phrases.notes: In other words, the word 'יהיה' only teaches the age rule, not the rule about having no blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 19 by limiting the ברייתא from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'יהיה' requires the animal to be both תמים and בן שנה through זריקה, which would clash with רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יהיה' only requires the animal to be בן שנה through זריקה. Being תמים is not required at that point.

steps.title: How can an animal age a year between שחיטה and זריקה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how an animal could be בן שנה at שחיטה but already in its second year at הולכה and זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there really a case where the animal is in its first year at the time of slaughter, but in its second year at the time of carrying and sprinkling the blood?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It seems impossible for the animal's age to change in the short time between שחיטה and זריקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the derivation is only about age, it should be useless, because the blood service happens right after the שחיטה. A whole year cannot pass in a few minutes. So why would the תורה need to teach that the animal must be בן שנה during הולכה and זריקה?

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying the blood to the מזבח
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: But is there anything
that at the time of slaughter is in its first year,
but at the time of carrying and sprinkling is in its second year?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20 as describing a case that seems impossible.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that 'יהיה' only teaches the age requirement through זריקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The time between שחיטה and זריקה is too short for the animal to pass from its first year into its second, so the derivation would teach nothing.

steps.title: Age is counted by the hour
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from this that hours matter for קדשים. The animal's year ends at the exact hour it was born, so it can turn two between שחיטה and זריקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches that hours disqualify in קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. He says this derivation shows that an animal's age is counted down to the exact hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year is not counted by whole days. It ends at the exact hour of the animal's birth. So if the animal was born at a certain hour exactly one year earlier, that hour can pass between the שחיטה and the זריקה, and the animal becomes פסול.
steps.whatToRemember: The word 'יהיה' teaches that a קרבן פסח must still be בן שנה through זריקה, and its age is counted to the exact hour (שעות פוסלות בקדשים).
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general rule for the age limits of all קרבנות: the year ends at the hour of birth, not at the end of the day.

phrases.english: Rava said: This teaches
that hours disqualify in sacrificial animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by showing that the case is possible.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the case is possible by setting out a new rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An animal cannot pass from its first year to its second during the blood service.
steps.terutzMaskana: Age is measured by the hour, so the animal can turn two between שחיטה and זריקה.

steps.title: Animal inside, legs outside: cutting the legs before slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי quotes רבי אלעזר: if an animal stands inside the עזרה with its legs outside, and one cut off its legs and then slaughtered it, the קרבן is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said in the name of רבי אלעזר: If the animal is inside and its legs are outside, and he cut off the legs and afterwards slaughtered it, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement about an animal whose body is in the עזרה but whose legs stick out of it. The statement continues after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the legs that were outside the עזרה are cut off first. So when the שחיטה happens, the whole animal that is left is inside, and the קרבן is fit. The order matters: the cutting came before the slaughter.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Elazar said:
If it is inside and its legs are outside;
phrases.notes: 'Inside' and 'outside' mean inside and outside the עזרה, the courtyard of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: if he cut off the legs and afterwards slaughtered it, it is fit,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement after רבא's conclusion. It is a new topic: an animal that is partly outside the עזרה at the time of שחיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal standing inside the עזרה with its legs outside, whose legs were cut off before שחיטה, is fit.
